speaker: Elder Maren
before: Come and find me on the square once you've dried off. When you're ready for the roads, I'll send you out myself.
after: Come and find me at my house once you've dried off. When you're ready for the roads, I'll send you out myself.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: That's my secret, and now you're holding it, the same way I have been holding yours. You may do with it as you see fit.
after: That's my secret, and now you're holding it. Do with it as you see fit.

speaker: (narration/UI)
before: A boy of eleven stands in a coat too fine for the cold, and someone is calling to him across a courtyard: '{prince}!'
after: A boy of eleven stands in a worn cloak too thin for the cold, and someone is calling to him across a courtyard: '{prince}!'

speaker: The Wanderer
before: My mother called to me across that courtyard. I can hear her voice now, and I still can't see her face. I'd like to, one day. I'd like to know what the two of them were like.
after: My mother called to me across that courtyard. I can hear her voice now, and I can see her face. I'd like to know what the two of them were like.

speaker: The Rescuer (Elowen)
before: Don't look so surprised. I told you somebody had to watch the door while you knocked it down.
after: Don't look so surprised. Somebody had to watch the door while you knocked it down. {rescuer}. It's {rescuer}. I promised.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: {rescuer}. Her name is {rescuer}. I asked her twice, and both times she said 'a friend', and both times I let her leave it at that.
after: {rescuer}. She told me her name with the guards already running at her, because she had promised me it would come first.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: I met a man who was locked up for ten years without a single weight, and he could still lift me off the floor. Strength is what you do with whatever is left to you, and strength is not control.
after: Ten years of 'again', every single morning. I learned to hear a different word in it each day: not yet. You never once heard it.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: You copied my cards, but what I do with them is mine. I watched a cook give her own name away and stay exactly who she was, so I know a name is a blank page until you sign it.
after: You copied my cards, but what I do with them is mine. Every choice I made in that dark, I made myself, and you cannot copy a choice.

speaker: The Wanderer

after: You copied my cards, but what I do with them is mine. Every choice I made in that dark, I made myself, and you cannot copy a choice.

speaker: (narration)
before: Four banners fly from the same pole. It is a little crowded, and nobody minds.
after: Four banners fly side by side over the square. It is a little crowded, and nobody minds.
